title: GradientDependentHessian.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a C³ function f:E→ℝ, permitting nonconvex objectives. The initial objective gap satisfies f(x₀)−inf f≤Δ, and ‖∇f(x₀)‖≤G₀. No convexity or gradient-dominance condition is imposed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns the full exact gradient ∇f(x) at any queried point, independently of the call index and seed. Gradient calls have a separate fixed budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GradientDependentHessian.lean: spec.admissible, oracle-0 equality; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the full exact Hessian D(∇f)(x) as a continuous linear operator, independently of the call index and seed. Hessian calls have a separate fixed budget. Function values are not supplied by either oracle.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GradientDependentHessian.lean: spec.numOracles, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible, oracle-1 equality; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The pointwise third-derivative bound ‖D²(∇f)(x)‖≤L₀+L₁‖∇f(x)‖ holds globally, with L₀>0 and L₁≥0. This controls variation of the Hessian; it is not a bound on the Hessian norm itself.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All parameters are public: E, x₀, L₀, L₁, Δ, G₀, ε, and m. Their restrictions are L₀>0, L₁≥0, Δ>0, G₀≥0, ε>0, and integer m≥1. The objective f is the hidden instance. The parameter m affects the supplied oracle budgets but imposes no additional condition on f.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GradientDependentHessian.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return a point x∈E satisfying ‖∇f(x)‖≤ε. The criterion uses the norm, not its square, and requires neither objective accuracy nor second-order stationarity.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The output criterion must hold almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within the separate fixed oracle budgets. Deterministic algorithm behavior is not required.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GradientDependentHessian.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.law, Oracle.law, execute, and Convergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup uses gradient-dependent control of the third derivative instead of uniform Hessian Lipschitz continuity, with separately budgeted exact gradient and full-Hessian access.

descriptionHtml:
Stationarity with Gradient-Dependent Third Derivatives

We consider a possibly nonconvex objective f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The function is three times continuously differentiable, with its third derivative bounded by L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥ at each x∈E, where L0>0 and L1≥0. A given starting point x0∈E has objective gap at most Δ>0 above the infimum and gradient norm at most G0≥0. Two exact oracles return the gradient and Hessian. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and derivative norms ∥⋅∥op are the induced operator norms. The algorithm receives E, x0, L0, L1, Δ, G0, ε, and an integer m≥1.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Third-derivative bound). The function f belongs to C3(E;R) and satisfies ∥∇3f(x)∥op≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥,x∈E. Here ∇3f(x) denotes the trilinear third derivative of f, equivalently the second derivative of its gradient under the inner product identification.

Assumption 2 (Initial bounds). The given point x0 satisfies f(x0)−f(x)≤Δfor every x∈E,∥∇f(x0)∥≤G0.

Queries to either oracle may be made at any point of E. The gradient oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. The Hessian oracle returns ∇2f(x) at x, as a linear operator from E to E. Gradient and Hessian calls are counted separately.

After the allotted calls to each oracle, the output must satisfy ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f∈C3 satisfies ∥∇3f(x)∥≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥ and f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ for every x, with ∥∇f(x0)∥≤G0. Here L0,Δ,ε>0, L1,G0≥0, and m∈N, m≥1. Exact gradient and Hessian oracles are available. The target is ∥∇f(xout)∥≤ε; (1) attains it deterministically.

Comparison for GradientDependentHessian.

(3) LazyCRN (Doikov et al. 2023), Thm. 3.1, Cor. 3.7 O(m+mL0Δε−3/2)
Special case: L1=0, globally L0-Lipschitz Hessian.		 (1): Scope extends Hessian reuse to gradient-dependent third derivatives, including unbounded Hessian variation. Matches known rate at L1=0. Abbr: Costs are Ng+mNH, with m gradient units per Hessian call; function-value calls in (2) cost one unit each and are included. A=Δ(L0ε−3/2+L1ε−1), ℓ=1+log⁡(1+L1G0/(mL0)). J=1+log+(max{σinit,L1G0}/(L0+L13/2Δ))+log+((L0+L13/2Δ)/σinit), where σinit>0 is the initial cubic regularization in (2). log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t}, [t]+=max{0,t}; δ is the second-order tolerance and 1/∞=0. H denotes a global Lipschitz constant of ∇2f; Ng,NH count gradient and Hessian evaluations.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

namespace LongTails.Setups.GradientDependentHessian

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  x0 : E
  L₀ : ℝ
  L₁ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  G₀ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  m : ℕ

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 2
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E ⊕ (p.E →L[ℝ] p.E)
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L₀ ∧ 0 ≤ p.L₁ ∧ 0 < p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.G₀ ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 1 ≤ p.m
  admissible p f O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 3 f ∧
    (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f)) x‖ ≤ p.L₀ + p.L₁ * ‖gradient f x‖) ∧
    (∀ x, f p.x0 - f x ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ‖gradient f p.x0‖ ≤ p.G₀ ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = Sum.inl (gradient f x)) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (1, x) seed = Sum.inr (fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x))
  successful p f output P := ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.GradientDependentHessian
